newsitem.title: UK: European VGO steady to shade up on low avails.
newsitem.headline: European VGO steady to shade up on low avails.

text.p: European vacuum gas oil prices were notionally steady to a touch stronger by mid-week on low avails, with the trans-Atlantic arb shut due to few larger cargoes and backwardation in NYMEX gasoline futures, traders said.
They said in the absence of fresh deals levels for low sulphur VGO cargoes were in the $127/$130 fob a tonne range after deals late last week at just below the higher number.

A refiner said it was asking $125 fob for a cargo of lower quality 0.8 pct sulphur VGO out of Lavera. Two prospective buyers shied away recently, one saying the price was too high and the other citing a problem over the specifications, the refiner added.
Traders said the arbitrage window to the United States was shut at the moment, with no barrels seen to make up larger cargoes.
"The barrels to go trans-Atlantic are not there...The 40,000 tonne loaders are not there to make freight sense," one trader said.
A second trader seconded that view, saying: "You can pick up bits and pieces for smaller cargoes into Europe but not to the States".
"The arb is closed. I think the biggest problem with the arb to the States is the backwardation in the market between August and September on Mogas," he added.
